Only paymob_secret_key is restricted to base.group_system field group; the other credentials (paymob_account_country_id, paymob_public_key, paymob_hmac_key, paymob_api_key) are left ungrouped though the form password-masks the HMAC, API and secret keys.

views.note: xml_loc=79: payment.provider form inheritance (payment_provider_views.xml: Paymob account country + public/secret/HMAC/API keys shown only when code=='paymob', secret/HMAC/API password-masked, available_currency_ids forced readonly, plus a 'Synchronize With Paymob' button calling action_sync_paymob_payment_methods) + the QWeb redirect-form template payment_paymob_templates.xml (auto-submit form with method='get' to the per-country {api_url}/unifiedcheckout/ carrying publicKey + clientSecret as query params), plus data/payment_provider_data.xml wiring redirect_form_view_id. behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._get_specific_rendering_values -> server-to-server POST {api_url}/v1/intention/ (Bearer secret key) then GET redirect to {api_url}/unifiedcheckout/ (Paymob Unified Checkout, per-country host)
behavioral_notes.observation: Paymob is a hybrid acquirer: the redirect is preceded by a real server-to-server API call. _get_specific_rendering_values builds the intention payload via _paymob_prepare_payment_request_payload (special_reference=tx.reference, amount=to_minor_currency_units(amount,currency), currency=currency.name, payment_methods=[<method>+env]-suffixed integration names where env is 'live' when provider.state=='enabled' else 'test' -- 'omannet' additionally appends 'card', notification_url=/payment/paymob/webhook, redirection_url=/payment/paymob/return, and a billing_data block with first/last name, email, street, state, phone, country) and POSTs it to '/v1/intention/' via the parent engine's _send_api_request with is_client_request=True (so _build_request_headers sends Authorization: Bearer paymob_secret_key). On success it stores provider_reference=payment_data['id'] and reads client_secret, then returns api_url={base}/unifiedcheckout/ plus url_params={publicKey: paymob_public_key, clientSecret: client_secret}; the QWeb redirect_form (method='get') auto-submits the browser to Paymob's hosted Unified Checkout. On ValidationError the tx is _set_error and an empty dict returned. The per-country base host comes from _paymob_get_api_url -> https://{API_MAPPING[account_country]}.paymob.com (uae/accept/oman/pakistan/ksa). None of this S2S call nor the hosted handoff is visible in Python field/model metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.provider._build_request_headers / _paymob_fetch_access_token -> dual Bearer auth (secret key for client requests vs OAuth access token) over https://{prefix}.paymob.com
behavioral_notes.observation: models/payment_provider.py wires Paymob's outbound auth onto the parent engine: _build_request_url targets _paymob_get_api_url()+endpoint (the per-country https://{API_MAPPING[code]}.paymob.com selected from paymob_account_country_id), and _build_request_headers returns Authorization: Bearer <auth> where auth is paymob_secret_key when is_client_request=True (the intention/checkout creation), or a short-lived OAuth access token otherwise; a refresh-token request (is_refresh_token_request=True) sends an empty bearer. _paymob_fetch_access_token POSTs {api_key: paymob_api_key} to '/api/auth/tokens' to mint that hourly-expiring token. The merchant-config action action_sync_paymob_payment_methods uses the same channel: GET '/api/ecommerce/integrations' to list Paymob gateways, _match_paymob_payment_methods filters them (skipping Apple/Google Pay, moto and is_auth/saved-card gateways via const.PAYMENT_METHODS_MAPPING), then PUT '/api/ecommerce/integrations/{id}' to set each integration_name to '<method><live|test>'. _parse_response_error pulls response.text and surfaces a 'fields must be filled' message from the billing_data error. This three-way endpoint set (auth tokens, intention, integrations) and the secret-vs-token bearer split are pure code, invisible to metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: PaymobController.paymob_return_from_checkout (/payment/paymob/return, GET) + paymob_webhook (/payment/paymob/webhook, POST) -> _verify_signature (HMAC SHA-512) BEFORE _process; reference via _extract_reference -> merchant_order_id
behavioral_notes.observation: Both public routes locate the tx with payment.transaction._search_by_reference('paymob', data) (routing through _extract_reference -> data['merchant_order_id']) then call _verify_signature BEFORE _process. The GET return route reads Paymob's flat query params directly; the POST csrf=False webhook reads request.get_json_data()['obj'] and first runs _normalize_response, which projects the nested webhook object onto the flat const.SIGNATURE_FIELDS shape (json-dumping booleans, str-defaulting missing values to 'false', flattening order.id / order.merchant_order_id / source_data.*) and carries the hmac from the query string. _verify_signature reads received=data['hmac'] (raising werkzeug Forbidden -> HTTP 403 if missing) and recomputes the expected value via _compute_signature: it CONCATENATES, with no separator and in the fixed const.SIGNATURE_FIELDS order (amount_cents, created_at, currency, error_occured, has_parent_transaction, id, integration_id, is_3d_secure, is_auth, is_capture, is_refunded, is_standalone_payment, is_voided, order, owner, pending, source_data.pan, source_data.sub_type, source_data.type, success -- each defaulting to 'false'), then hmac.new(paymob_hmac_key, signing_string, hashlib.sha512).hexdigest(); it rejects (Forbidden) unless hmac.compare_digest matches. This concatenated-in-list-order HMAC-SHA-512 (not sorted, not an SHA-256) and the constant-time compare are pure controller semantics, not derivable from metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._apply_updates / _extract_amount_data -> Paymob payment status -> payment state mapping
behavioral_notes.observation: _apply_updates maps Paymob's boolean-string flags into payment's guarded transitions: payment_data['pending']=='true' -> _set_pending; else payment_data['success']=='true' -> _set_done; otherwise _set_error carrying payment_data['data.message']. There is NO _set_canceled branch -- failures and cancellations both fall through to the error bucket. _extract_amount_data converts payment_data['amount_cents'] back to major units via to_major_currency_units and returns currency_code=payment_data['currency'] for the engine's amount cross-check. provider_reference is the intention id set at rendering time (data['id']); the webhook's flattened 'order' / 'merchant_order_id' are used only for lookup, not as the provider reference. This inbound flag->state translation is pure code, not visible in metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.provider currency binding -> one currency per Paymob account, matched to the account country
behavioral_notes.observation: Unlike most acquirers Paymob pins exactly ONE currency per provider. _inverse_paymob_account_country_id sets available_currency_ids (Command.set) to the single res.currency whose name is const.CURRENCY_MAPPING[account_country] (AE->AED, EG->EGP, OM->OMR, PK->PKR, SA->SAR), and the @api.constrains _check_available_country_currency_ids rejects (ValidationError) any provider with more than one available currency or a currency outside const.CURRENCY_MAPPING.values(). The form also forces available_currency_ids readonly for code=='paymob'. _get_default_payment_method_codes returns const.DEFAULT_PAYMENT_METHOD_CODES ({'card'}) on activation; const.PAYMENT_METHODS_MAPPING covers MENA methods (card, mobile_wallet_eg, kiosk, halan, sympl, valu, aman, souhoola, contact, premium_card, forsa, tabby, tamara, stcpay, omannet, easypaisa, jazzcash). This single-currency, country-pinned binding is enforced in code, not visible as plain field metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: external integration surface (gap #7) -- endpoints, keys, no SDK
behavioral_notes.observation: Static gap-#7 facts (extract_frontend.py): uses_api_keys=true; the declared endpoint template is the per-country https://{api_prefix}.paymob.com (api_prefix in uae/accept/oman/pakistan/ksa, chosen by paymob_account_country_id) declared in models/payment_provider.py (_build_request_url -> _paymob_get_api_url). Concrete endpoints reached server-to-server: /api/auth/tokens (OAuth access token from paymob_api_key), /v1/intention/ (Intention/Unified Checkout creation, Bearer paymob_secret_key), and /api/ecommerce/integrations[/{id}] (GET+PUT during the merchant payment-method sync). The buyer is then redirected (browser GET) to {base}/unifiedcheckout/ carrying publicKey + clientSecret, where card/wallet data are collected on Paymob's hosted page -- never in Odoo. There is no python SDK import and no browser SDK: HTTP is delegated to payment.provider._send_api_request, configured here via _build_request_url / _build_request_headers / _parse_response_error overrides. Authenticity of the inbound return/webhook rests on the HMAC SHA-512 over paymob_hmac_key. This server-to-server-then-hosted-redirect acquirer link is the canonical metadata gap #7: none of the Paymob endpoints, the secret/api-key bearer auth, the HMAC scheme, or the hosted-checkout handoff are reachable from model/field metadata.

0 JS files, 0 OWL components, 0 registry adds, 0 patches (gap #3). payment_paymob ships no client-side code and registers no web.assets_frontend bundle: the entire buyer interaction is the server-rendered redirect_form QWeb template (payment_paymob_templates.xml) whose hidden inputs auto-submit (method='get') to Paymob's hosted Unified Checkout. There is no browser SDK and no inline card form -- card/wallet data are collected on Paymob's hosted page, never in Odoo. The only browser-visible artifact is the auto-submitting redirect form (plain server-rendered HTML, no gap-#3 JS surface).

external_integrations.pattern: Concrete realization of metadata gap #7: a real external acquirer integration in a hybrid server-to-server-plus-hosted-redirect form. Outbound REST to the per-country {prefix}.paymob.com (auth-token, intention creation, integration sync) authenticated with a secret key / OAuth bearer; the browser is then GET-redirected to Paymob's hosted Unified Checkout (publicKey + clientSecret) so card/wallet data never touch Odoo; inbound settlement via an HMAC-SHA-512-verified return route plus a JSON webhook. Unlike pure redirect acquirers (APS, Buckaroo) Paymob makes a genuine S2S call to mint the checkout, but unlike Stripe/Xendit it captures no card in Odoo and stores no token. The base 'payment' engine ships no live acquirer; this module is exactly that override.
external_integrations.note: Gap-#7 example: none of the Paymob endpoints, the secret-key/OAuth bearer split, the HMAC-SHA-512 callback signing, or the hosted Unified Checkout handoff are derivable from Python model/field metadata; they were established only by reading const.py + payment_provider.py + payment_transaction.py + controllers/main.py.

Server-side Intention/Unified-Checkout creation then signed-redirect settlement (HMAC SHA-512) with no card data in Odoo
Single-currency-per-account acceptance pinned to the Paymob account country (AED / EGP / OMR / PKR / SAR)
Self-service payment-method synchronization with the Paymob portal (action_sync_paymob_payment_methods)

Configure-Methods: action_sync_paymob_payment_methods -> GET /api/ecommerce/integrations -> _match_paymob_payment_methods -> PUT integration_name per gateway so Paymob routes each Odoo method correctly
Settle: success=='true' -> _set_done -> downstream post-process settlement (account_payment / sale)

classification.apqc_category: 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (9.5 process payments / collect cash; manage external payment provider)
classification.rationale: payment_paymob is a value-NETWORK (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating-technology) component: a concrete acquirer adapter whose purpose is to interconnect two parties who would not otherwise transact directly -- the MENA-region cardholder / wallet user and the merchant -- by linking the merchant to Paymob's Egyptian/MENA payment network. It exhibits the mediating-technology activities: network promotion & contract management (account-country, public/secret/HMAC/API key management, single-currency enablement, and the action_sync_paymob_payment_methods portal synchronization), service provisioning (the per-transaction server-to-server Intention call that mints the Unified Checkout, then confirming the signed feedback), and infrastructure operation (the {prefix}.paymob.com REST link, the hosted Unified Checkout handoff, and the HMAC-SHA-512-verified return/webhook settlement loop). It does not transform inputs into outputs (chain) nor solve a bespoke customer problem (shop). It inherits the parent 'payment' engine's value_model exactly: the engine is the generic mediator and this module is its Paymob realization. activity_class is 'support' because, from the enterprise value-chain perspective, payment acceptance is an infrastructure/finance support function (category Accounting/Payment Providers, application=False, no end-user app) sitting under 9.0 Manage Financial Resources -- specifically 9.5 process payments / collect cash, with the side of 'manage an external payment provider'. So value_model=network (its own internal logic is mediation, an acquirer integration -- gap #7), activity_class=support (its place on the enterprise value chain). This mirrors the sibling payment_stripe / payment_xendit / payment_aps metamodels (network/support) and the parent payment engine; Paymob sits between pure redirect acquirers (APS, Buckaroo) and S2S acquirers (Stripe, Xendit) -- it makes a real S2S Intention call but still hands the buyer to a hosted checkout and holds no card or token.

standard_capabilities: server-to-server Intention creation then hosted-redirect payment via Paymob's Unified Checkout (per-country {prefix}.paymob.com, live vs test by provider.state)
MENA payment-method routing (card, mobile wallet, kiosk, BNPL/instalments: valU/Aman/Souhoola/Forsa/Tabby/Tamara/Halan/Sympl/Contact/STC Pay/OmanNet/EasyPaisa/JazzCash) mapped to Paymob gateway types
signed-redirect integrity and signature-verified settlement via an HMAC-SHA-512 hash over const.SIGNATURE_FIELDS + the HMAC key
asynchronous settlement via an HMAC-verified JSON webhook plus an (also HMAC-verified, GET) redirect-return route
single-currency-per-account acceptance pinned to the account country (AED/EGP/OMR/PKR/SAR)
self-service payment-method synchronization with the Paymob portal (GET/PUT /api/ecommerce/integrations)
typical_fits: online shop / portal checkout collecting card or local-method payments in Egypt and the wider MENA region via Paymob
BNPL / instalment acceptance (valU, Aman, Souhoola, Forsa, Tabby, Tamara) routed through Paymob gateways
send-a-payment-link or pay-an-invoice-online collection (with account_payment / sale downstream)
merchants needing card/wallet acceptance without holding card data (Paymob-hosted Unified Checkout, nothing entered in Odoo)
common_gaps: no tokenization / saved cards (saved-card gateways are explicitly filtered out during sync) -- every payment is a fresh checkout
no manual capture / authorize-then-capture (moto and is_auth gateways are filtered out) and no void operation
no in-module refund operation (no _send_refund_request override here)
no explicit cancel-state mapping (only pending and success are handled; everything else, including cancellations, falls through to _set_error)
Apple Pay and Google Pay gateways are not supported (skipped during sync)
exactly one currency per provider, pinned to the account country -- a merchant operating multiple currencies needs multiple Paymob providers
the public-URL requirement for the return/webhook means local/dev instances need a tunnel; without the HMAC key set, signature verification has no secret to compare against
bespoke reconciliation / settlement document chains live downstream (account_payment, sale), not here

open_questions: Exact Paymob Intention API request/response payloads and Unified Checkout feedback field sets beyond those built in _paymob_prepare_payment_request_payload / read in _apply_updates (id, client_secret, amount_cents, currency, pending, success, data.message, merchant_order_id).
Real-world distribution of Paymob transaction states and method mix (card vs wallet vs BNPL) across the five supported countries -- no runtime row counts captured.
How refunds / cancellations are handled operationally given no in-module refund override and no cancel-state mapping (likely via the Paymob dashboard or a downstream module).
Whether instances reliably register/receive the webhook vs rely on the (also HMAC-verified) GET return route, and whether both can fire for the same transaction.
